mainTopic: The warning for cursing with ה׳'s name, and the dispute over lashes for separating תרומה before ביכורים
overview: The גמרא finishes proving that the punishment verse in דברים 28 is about cursing another person with ה׳'s name. Only cursing has a clear לאו behind it: 'לא תקלל חרש'. A challenge from 'את ה׳ אלהיך תירא' is pushed off, because a positive command (עשה) cannot serve as the warning. The גמרא then explains רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא's ruling that one who separates תרומה before ביכורים gets lashes. His source is 'מלאתך ודמעך לא תאחר'. Next comes a dispute between רבי אלעזר and רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא over whether he gets lashes. The גמרא first assigns 'lashes' to רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא. Then, using רבי אלעזר's ruling on a משנה about tithing two baskets out of order, it concludes that רבי אלעזר is the one who says 'lashes'. That leaves רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא seeming to contradict himself, and the answer to this begins here and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The punishment verse must be about cursing a fellow Jew
steps.stepSummary: The verse giving the punishment cannot be about saying ה׳'s name in vain, because that sin would have no לאו to warn against it. Cursing a fellow Jew does have a לאו: 'לא תקלל חרש'.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can't say the verse is about saying ה׳'s name in vain. It is written 'Do not curse the deaf.' If the verse is about cursing one's fellow, fine: its warning comes from 'Do not curse the deaf.' But if it is about saying ה׳'s name in vain, where is its warning?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge: the punishment verse (דברים 28:58-59) is about cursing another person with ה׳'s name, not about saying His name for no reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a sin to bring punishment, the תורה needs a punishment verse and also a separate warning, an אזהרה, in the form of a לאו. Cursing a fellow Jew has a ready לאו, 'לא תקלל חרש'. Saying ה׳'s name in vain seems to have no לאו, so the punishment verse cannot be about it.

keyTerms.meaning: You cannot say (that reading does not work)
A warning: the לאו that forbids an act, needed before a punishment can be given
'Do not curse the deaf': the לאו against cursing a fellow Jew
Granted, it works out well if…
Saying ה׳'s name for no purpose

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two verses. דברים 28 gives the punishment, and 'לא תקלל חרש' gives the warning. The תורה needs both before someone can be punished.

phrases.english: You cannot say [that the verse is about saying ה׳'s name in vain],
phrases.notes: The verse here is דברים 28:58-59, about ה׳'s punishment for not fearing His glorious name.

phrases.english: for it is written: "You shall not curse the deaf."

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי אָמְרַתְּ בִּשְׁלָמָא לְקַלֵּל אֶת חֲבֵירוֹ
phrases.english: Granted, if you say [the verse is about] cursing one's fellow,
its warning comes from here,
as it is written: "You shall not curse the deaf."

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִי אָמְרַתְּ מוֹצִיא שֵׁם שָׁמַיִם לְבַטָּלָה
phrases.english: But if you say [it is about] saying the name of Heaven in vain,
where does its warning come from?

steps.raayaObject: That the punishment verse in דברים 28 is about cursing another person with ה׳'s name
steps.raayaSupportSource: Cursing has a לאו ('לא תקלל חרש'), but saying ה׳'s name in vain seems to have none

steps.title: Challenge: fearing ה׳ could be the warning
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: saying ה׳'s name in vain does have a warning. The verse 'את ה׳ אלהיך תירא' tells us to fear ה׳.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why not? Isn't it written: 'You shall fear ה׳ your God, and Him you shall serve'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the last step's claim that saying ה׳'s name in vain has no warning verse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Fearing ה׳ surely includes not using His name carelessly. So 'את ה׳ אלהיך תירא' could serve as the warning, and then the punishment verse could be about saying His name in vain after all.

keyTerms.meaning: Why not? (what is the problem?)
But isn't it written…!
You shall fear (יראת שמים)

phrases.english: Why not?
But isn't it written:
"You shall fear ה׳ your God, and Him you shall serve"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the claim in step 1 that there is no warning for saying ה׳'s name in vain
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that מוציא שם שמים לבטלה has no אזהרה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The verse commanding fear of ה׳ already covers not using His name in vain, so it could be the warning

steps.title: A positive command does not count as a warning
steps.stepSummary: The 'fear ה׳' verse is phrased as a positive command (עשה). A warning for punishment has to be a לאו.
steps.simpleTranslation: That verse is a warning in the form of a positive command.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. 'את ה׳ אלהיך תירא' is an עשה, so it cannot be the warning needed for punishment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only a לאו, a 'do not', can be the אזהרה for a punishment. Since 'תירא' is worded as a command to do something, it does not count. So step 1's proof stands: the punishment verse is about cursing another person.

keyTerms.meaning: A 'warning' worded as a positive command, which does not count as a real אזהרה for punishment
A negative commandment ('do not…')

steps.whatToRemember: A punishment needs two things: a punishment verse and an אזהרה that is a לאו. A positive command (עשה) cannot be the אזהרה. That is why the punishment verse in דברים 28 is about cursing another person, which has the לאו 'לא תקלל חרש'.

phrases.english: That is a warning in the form of a positive command.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Defines the type of verse: an עשה cannot be an אזהרה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any verse that implies a prohibition, even a positive command, could be the warning
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a לאו can be an אזהרה for punishment, so 'תירא' does not count

steps.title: Quoting רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא on תרומה before ביכורים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings back an earlier statement in the name of רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא. Also one who separates תרומה before ביכורים is included among those who get lashes.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said in the name of רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא: also one who separates תרומה before ביכורים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new topic. It re-quotes a line from the previous daf so that it can now explain it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the גמרא listed special לאוין that bring lashes even though no action is done. רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא added one more case to that list: separating תרומה before ביכורים. The next steps will look for his source.

keyTerms.meaning: The portion of produce given to a כהן
First fruits brought to the בית המקדש
One who puts something earlier (separates it first)

phrases.aramaic: מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא אָמְרוּ:
phrases.english: They said in the name of Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Chanina:
Also one who separates terumah before bikkurim [gets lashes].

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא אָמְרוּ
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Separating תרומה before ביכורים is one of the לאוין that bring lashes

steps.title: What is his source?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what verse רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא bases his ruling on.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source of רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא's ruling. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Lashes need a לאו in the תורה. So the גמרא wants to know which verse forbids separating תרומה before ביכורים.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason / source?

phrases.aramaic: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא?
phrases.english: What is the reason of Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Chanina?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The verse behind the לאו against separating תרומה before ביכורים

steps.title: The verse: 'Your fullness and your outflow, do not delay'
steps.stepSummary: The verse in שמות 22:28 mentions 'fullness', meaning ביכורים, and then 'outflow', meaning תרומה. It then says 'do not delay', so ביכורים must not be pushed back behind תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'Your fullness and your outflow, do not delay.' 'Fullness' means ביכורים. 'Your outflow' means תרומה. And the verse says 'do not delay.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a verse. It reads it as setting an order: ביכורים first, then תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse names ביכורים before תרומה and adds 'לא תאחר', 'do not delay'. Separating תרומה first would delay the ביכורים, and that breaks a לאו. Because it is a לאו, it can bring lashes.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Fullness': read here as ביכורים
'Outflow': read here as תרומה
Do not delay

phrases.english: The verse says:
"Your fullness and your outflow you shall not delay"
"Fullness": this is bikkurim,
"and your outflow": this is terumah,
and the verse says "do not delay."
phrases.notes: Don't push the first thing in the verse (ביכורים) behind the second (תרומה).

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר קְרָא: מְלֵאָתְךָ וְדִמְעֲךָ לֹא תְאַחֵר
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: שמות 22:28: the order 'fullness' (ביכורים) then 'outflow' (תרומה), together with 'לא תאחר', makes a לאו against separating תרומה first

steps.title: A dispute: lashes or no lashes?
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר and רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא disagree about someone who separated תרומה before ביכורים. One says he gets lashes and one says he does not, but we are not told who holds which view.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: if someone separated תרומה before ביכורים, רבי אלעזר and רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא disagree. One said he gets lashes, and one said he does not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a recorded dispute about this case without saying which sage holds which view. This sets up the next step, which will try to match the opinions to the sages.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the ruling is not just one sage's statement. It is a real argument between two אמוראים. The open question is which of them holds which side.

keyTerms.meaning: He gets lashes (מלקות)
He does not get lashes
One said (the views are not tied to names)

phrases.english: It was stated:
If one separated terumah before bikkurim,

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא,
phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar and Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Chanina [disagree]:
one said: he gets lashes,
and one said: he does not get lashes.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two אמוראים disagree whether separating תרומה before ביכורים brings lashes, but the views are not tied to names

steps.title: So רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא is the one who says lashes
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא is the one who says 'he gets lashes'. We already know he said exactly that in the earlier statement.
steps.simpleTranslation: We can conclude that רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא is the one who said he gets lashes. After all, רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא said: also one who separates תרומה before ביכורים gets lashes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses the earlier quote to match the unnamed views. רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא says lashes, so רבי אלעזר must say no lashes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'תסתיים' (let us conclude) is a suggestion built on what we already know from step 4. Watch for whether the גמרא accepts this matching or questions it next.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us conclude / it can be shown

phrases.english: Conclude that it is Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Chanina
who said he gets lashes,
since Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Chanina said:
Also one who separates terumah before bikkurim gets lashes.

steps.triggerLanguage: תִּסְתַּיֵּים דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא הוּא דְּאָמַר לוֹקֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to match the unnamed views of step 7 to the two sages
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא holds 'לוקה' in the dispute
steps.raayaSupportSource: His earlier statement (step 4) that one who separates תרומה before ביכורים gets lashes

steps.title: On the contrary: a משנה about two baskets of untithed produce
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא flips the suggestion and argues that רבי אלעזר is the one who says 'he gets lashes.' It brings a משנה about tithing two baskets of טבל as the background.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the contrary, conclude that רבי אלעזר is the one who says 'he gets lashes.' We learned in a משנה: Someone had two baskets of untithed produce in front of him and said, 'The tithe of this one is in that one.' The first basket is now tithed. If he said, 'The tithe of this one is in that one, and the tithe of that one is in this one,' the first is tithed but the second is not. If he said, 'Their tithes: each basket's tithe is in the other,' he has made both declarations at once, and both are tithed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back against the last suggestion and sets up a proof that רבי אלעזר is the one who says 'he gets lashes.' First it quotes a משנה about tithing two baskets.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה teaches that order matters in tithing. Once the first basket has been tithed, it cannot be used as tithe for the second basket. This background prepares for רבי אלעזר's comment on the first case, which comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: On the contrary: the opposite of what was just suggested
Produce from which תרומה and מעשרות have not yet been taken
Basket
He has 'called the name,' meaning he made a valid declaration of the tithe

phrases.english: On the contrary, conclude
that it is Rabbi Elazar who says he gets lashes,
as we learned in a mishnah:
phrases.notes: This is the משנה in דמאי 7:6.

phrases.aramaic: הָיוּ לְפָנָיו שְׁתֵּי כַּלְכַּלּוֹת שֶׁל טֶבֶל,
phrases.english: If there were two baskets of untithed produce in front of him,
and he said: 'The tithe of this one is in that one,'
the first basket is tithed.
If he said: 'That of this one is in that one, and that of that one is in this one,'
the first is tithed, but the second is not tithed.
phrases.notes: The first basket was already tithed by his first words, so it can no longer serve as tithe for the second.

phrases.english: If he said: 'Their tithes: the tithe of each basket is in the other,'
he has called the name.
phrases.notes: He declared both tithes in a single statement, so both baskets count as tithed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַדְּרַבָּה, תִּסְתַּיֵּים דְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר הוּא דְּאָמַר לוֹקֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reverses Step 8's suggestion and begins a counter-proof.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי אלעזר is the one who says 'he gets lashes'
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה דמאי 7:6 about two baskets of טבל

steps.title: רבי אלעזר rules lashes for tithing out of order
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר says that in the first case of the משנה the person gets lashes, because he separated מעשר שני before מעשר ראשון. The גמרא concludes that he is the one who says 'he gets lashes.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And it was said: רבי אלעזר says he gets lashes, because he separated the מעשר שני of this basket before the מעשר ראשון of the other basket. Conclude from this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its proof. רבי אלעזר gives lashes for taking tithes out of order, so he must also be the one who gives lashes for taking תרומה before ביכורים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Taking מעשר שני before מעשר ראשון breaks the same rule of 'do not delay' as taking תרומה before ביכורים. Since רבי אלעזר gives lashes in the tithe case, he very likely gives lashes in the ביכורים case too. The גמרא accepts this with תסתיים.

keyTerms.meaning: First tithe, given to the לוי
Second tithe, eaten in ירושלים
He put first: he did something earlier than its proper turn

phrases.english: And it was stated: Rabbi Elazar says he gets lashes,
phrases.notes: He's talking about the first case of the משנה: 'the tithe of this one is in that one.'

phrases.english: because he put the second tithe of this one first
before the first tithe of the other one.
Conclude it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies רבי אלעזר's ruling on the משנה from Step 9, which completes the proof.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי אלעזר says 'he gets lashes' for separating out of order
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי אלעזר's ruling on the first case of the משנה in דמאי
steps.whyThisMatters: It ties the ביכורים/תרומה dispute to the general rule of separating gifts in the right order.

steps.title: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא now seems to contradict himself
steps.stepSummary: If רבי אלעזר says 'he gets lashes,' then רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא says 'he does not get lashes.' That clashes with his earlier statement that one who separates תרומה before ביכורים does get lashes.
steps.simpleTranslation: But then רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא is the one who says 'he does not get lashes.' Shall we say that רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא contradicts רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a problem that comes from the last conclusion. רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא now seems to say two opposite things, and this sets up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 4 רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא clearly said that one who separates תרומה before ביכורים gets lashes. If the opinion 'he does not get lashes' now belongs to him, his two statements clash. The word לימא shows the גמרא is raising the problem, and it expects to resolve it.

keyTerms.meaning: A difficulty / contradiction
Shall we say: it raises a possibility that the גמרא usually goes on to reject

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two statements. Earlier (Step 4) רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא said 'he gets lashes.' The contradiction exists only because the dispute in Step 7 would now give him the opposite view.

phrases.english: But then Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Chanina
is the one who says he does not get lashes;

phrases.aramaic: לֵימָא קַשְׁיָא דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא
phrases.english: shall we say there is a contradiction of Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Chanina
against Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Chanina!
phrases.notes: This is his own earlier statement from Step 4, that one who takes תרומה before ביכורים gets lashes.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵימָא קַשְׁיָא דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא אַדְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the cost of Step 10's conclusion: it leaves רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא contradicting himself.
steps.kashyaTarget: The conclusion that רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא holds 'he does not get lashes'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: This would contradict his own earlier statement (Step 4) that one who separates תרומה before ביכורים gets lashes.

steps.title: The answer begins: rethinking the earlier statement
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the contradiction with the word 'No' and starts to explain what רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא meant in his earlier statement about תרומה before ביכורים.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא, when he said that earlier statement, [was speaking in a specific way, explained next].
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins to answer the contradiction from step 11 by saying 'No.' This line only sets up the answer, and the explanation itself comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word לָא tells us that the contradiction is not a real one. The גמרא now focuses on רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא's earlier statement, which said that one who separates תרומה before ביכורים gets lashes. It is getting ready to show that this statement does not have to clash with his view in the מחלוקת with רבי אלעזר.

keyTerms.meaning: 'No.' It opens an answer by rejecting the challenge just raised.
Separating תרומה before ביכורים, the earlier statement now being explained

steps.confusionAlert: Don't stop here thinking the answer is finished. This line only opens the answer. The actual explanation of רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא's statement comes on the next amud.

phrases.english: No, Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Ḥanina,
phrases.notes: The גמרא is starting to explain his earlier statement about תרומה before ביכורים. The sentence continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the answer to the contradiction raised in step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading the earlier statement of רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא (the details follow on the next amud)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: His earlier statement that one who separates תרומה before ביכורים gets lashes is his own fixed view, so it contradicts the view that he does not get lashes.
steps.terutzMaskana: The answer begins by denying the contradiction. The explanation of how his earlier statement fits comes on the next amud.
